summary.oneLiner: Kajaria leveraged the Morbi cluster shutdown (due to gas shortages) and prior sales unification efforts to drive 11% volume growth and expand EBITDA margins to 19.2% via price hikes, positioning itself to capture significant market share as unorganized competitors face structural cost disadvantages. While Q1 faces transient production lags from the Morbi restart, the medium-term outlook favors consolidated players with multi-location assets and biofuel flexibility.

one-line thesis: Kajaria leveraged the Morbi cluster shutdown (due to gas shortages) and prior sales unification efforts to drive 11% volume growth and expand EBITDA margins to 19.2% via price hikes, positioning itself to capture significant market share as unorganized competitors face structural cost disadvantages. While Q1 faces transient production lags from the Morbi restart, the medium-term outlook favors consolidated players with multi-location assets and biofuel flexibility.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 1,373 cr (+12% YoY); EBITDA: INR 263 cr (Margin 19.19% vs 10.01% YoY); PAT: INR 136 cr (+216% YoY) driven by volume mix and realization; Order Book: Not disclosed (Make-to-Stock model); Net Debt: Net Cash position (implied by buyback rationale and working capital improvement); One-offs: Morbi plant shutdown in March reduced production by 7% despite sales growth; Accounting note: Presentation error corrected swapping inventory/debtors figures.
guidance: Revenue Growth: No specific guidance given (management cites external volatility); Margin: Targeting 18-19% range; Order Inflow: Momentum positive post-Jan '26, Q1 seasonally weak but YoY April expected strong; Capex/Commissioning: Morbi plants restarted April 16; full capacity running.
order book & pipeline: N/A (Inventory-driven model); Finished Goods Inventory reduced by ~1.5 million sqm in March to ~11 million sqm total; Days Sales Inventory improved significantly contributing to 14-day reduction in working capital cycle (51 days).
segment / subsidiary detail: Tiles: INR 1,212 cr (+11% YoY); Bathware: INR 117 cr (+6% YoY); Adhesives: INR 44 cr (+110% YoY). Tiles remain core driver; Adhesives showing high base growth.
growth verticals / optionality: Market share gain from Morbi unorganized cluster (estimated 150-160 plants running vs 500+ previously); Adhesive segment scaling; Potential for further pricing power as cost differential widens for competitors.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expanded to 19.19% (vs 10.01% YoY) due to 12-17% price hikes covering gas inflation; Fuel cost mix: North ~INR 62.5/scm (April), South/West ~INR 79-81/scm; Biofuel usage ~15-30% in North spray dryers providing cost arbitrage vs pure gas players.
capex / expansion: No major greenfield capex announced; Focus on restarting Morbi JV/outsourced capacity; Maintenance capex ongoing.
capital allocation: Buyback approved to return surplus cash (tax-efficient vs dividends) and improve ROE; Working capital optimization priority (cycle down to 51 days).
risks & watch-items: Sustained high gas prices impacting demand elasticity; Propane ban permanence for industry; Morbi competitors restarting faster than expected; Geopolitical impact on freight costs (UAE freight up to $4k) hurting export potential.
management quality / tone: Confident and opportunistic regarding competitor distress; Cautious on providing specific numerical guidance due to macro volatility; Emphasizes structural advantage of multi-location footprint.
non-obvious takeaways: Management highlighted that Morbi competitors face a 35-40% cost hike (vs Kajaria's 15-16% price increase) due to lower base prices and higher gas dependency, creating a permanent margin gap; Export market effectively closed for Morbi due to freight spikes ($300 to $4000 to UAE), forcing all supply into domestic market but at uncompetitive prices.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gas price surge (INR 47 to INR 84/scm) and propane ban shutting down unorganized Morbi clusters; inability to pass on 35-40% cost increases without losing volume. | Somany Ceramics | beneficiary | High | Multi-location player similar to Kajaria; benefits from same supply vacuum and pricing power in North/West markets. |
| High exposure to Morbi cluster disruptions and lack of biofuel/alternative fuel infrastructure compared to organized peers. | Unlisted Morbi Manufacturers | loser | High | Facing existential cost crisis; many plants remain shut or operating at low utilization; forced to raise prices 35-40% which demand may not bear. |

themes.title: Building-materials & home-improvement up-cycle
themes.need: The residential up-cycle pulls a broad finishing/home-improvement basket - tiles & sanitaryware (KAJARIACER/CERA/SOMANYCERA/ORIENTBELL/HINDWAREAP), wood-panels & laminates (CENTURYPLY/GREENPANEL/GREENLAM/RUSHIL/STYLAMIND), pipes/adhesives (PIDILITIND/SUPREMEIND/ASTRAL-tier) and paints (ASIANPAINT/CARYSIL/SIRCA). Premiumization + GST formalization shift share to organized players.
themes.driver: Festive/real-estate completion demand; GST 2.0 + commodity tailwinds; capacity commissioning and channel restocking.
